Subject: Major latency spike / partial downtime this AM (05/20) - impact on production

Hi Ben,

We experienced a major spike this morning between ~09:05–09:34 PT where requests to your inference endpoint (model: rdx-1.3-large) either timed out or returned 500 errors. We saw ~12% of requests failing and end-to-end latency jump from ~220ms to ~4s for the bulk of that window. This affected our recommendation pipeline and a few customer-facing workflows; we estimate ~1% of active sessions dropped or queued and one batch job failed to process.

I've attached an error log excerpt and our internal incident notes. Our CTO wants to know what happened and is asking for a remediation plan plus a goodwill credit / trial extension while we validate the next billing cycle. Can you confirm:
- root cause and whether Redwood has a lasting remediation plan?
- what compensation you're able to provide for the impact?

We appreciate a prompt reply; the incident is blocking our QA sign-off for an upcoming release.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations
Starline

Marta —

Thanks again for the patience while we investigated. We’ve completed the review: transient request queuing in our autoscaler caused the latency spike when a maintenance task overlapped a burst of requests. The engineering team has pushed a fix to the autoscaler config and we’ve added a regression test to prevent recurrence. Detailed postmortem will follow in the support ticket.

As discussed and approved internally, Redwood will provide the following remediation package:
- One-time platform credit of USD 5,000 applied to Starline (visible on next invoice).
- 30-day extension of your trial window for Dedicated features (no charge).

Attached: authorized_credit_note_0522.pdf (formal credit memo). Please reply to confirm acceptance and we’ll apply the credit. If you’d like the credit applied immediately to an outstanding invoice, let me know the invoice number and we’ll route to billing.

We’ve also scheduled a 30-minute postmortem with engineering for Tue 05/25 — invite to follow.

Appreciate the partnership, and we’ll keep you updated on the postmortem detail.
